findings.affectedRouteOrComponent: Dashboard theme editor and style reference
findings.currentBehavior: Theme metadata, defaults, CSS variable emitters, editor controls, and style-reference documentation were split across separate structures.
findings.problem: Separate token lists make it easy for emitted variables, editor controls, and documentation to drift.
findings.accessibilityOrUsabilityImpact: Admins may edit a palette without seeing every rendered or compatibility value that affects contrast, focus, and component states.
findings.recommendedChange: Use the canonical DASHBOARD_THEME_TOKEN_REGISTRY as the shared metadata source and gate it with coverage tests.

findings.currentBehavior: The global stylesheet is 5679 lines and still contains base rules, admin layout, charts, style reference, modals, QR controls, responsive rules, and compatibility overrides. This branch adds focused admin-data.css and admin-theme-editor.css layers for new table and editor contracts.
findings.problem: A single high-volume stylesheet still increases cascade risk, duplicate selectors, and review difficulty, though new visual-system work now has focused CSS entry points.
findings.accessibilityOrUsabilityImpact: Small changes can unintentionally affect focus, density, and responsive behavior across unrelated screens.
findings.recommendedChange: Continue extracting globals by component family after screenshot coverage, preserving custom-property contracts and the new focused table/editor layers.

findings.currentBehavior: The generated redirect fallback document previously contained its own hard-coded light and dark color palette; this branch derives it from DEFAULT_DASHBOARD_THEME.
findings.problem: The fallback page can visually drift from the admin theme and custom palette because it does not consume the dashboard token registry.
findings.accessibilityOrUsabilityImpact: Contrast and brand consistency can diverge on error or redirect states, which are high-friction moments.
findings.recommendedChange: Keep redirect fallback CSS derived from registry defaults or a sanitized exported palette rather than copying colors.
findings.relevantThemeToken: background, surface, text, muted, border, accent, shadowColor

findings.affectedRouteOrComponent: Typography, spacing, radius, shadows, layout widths
findings.currentBehavior: Control height and padding are tokenized, and this branch adds a read-only structural visual-token registry for typography, spacing, radius, controls, tables, shadows, motion, layers, and breakpoints.
findings.problem: Only color remains deeply editable; structural values are documented and tested but intentionally not yet user-editable.
findings.accessibilityOrUsabilityImpact: Density and touch targets can drift between pages and make text resizing or mobile use less predictable.
findings.recommendedChange: Keep structural tokens read-only until a narrower migration can safely promote spacing, radius, and type controls to editable settings.
findings.relevantThemeToken: Proposed: space.*, radius.*, type.*, shadow.*, z.*

findings.currentBehavior: Transitions and one keyframe animation are defined; this branch adds prefers-reduced-motion handling that disables nonessential motion.
findings.problem: Users who request reduced motion still receive opacity/transform transitions and highlight pulses.
findings.accessibilityOrUsabilityImpact: Motion-sensitive users may experience discomfort, and focus highlight animation can be distracting.
findings.recommendedChange: Keep the global reduced-motion media query and include it in future screenshot/a11y checks.

findings.currentBehavior: This branch adds forced-colors rules for core controls, surfaces, tables, focus, and feedback primitives.
findings.problem: Custom backgrounds, borders, and focus rings may not adapt well in Windows High Contrast or user contrast modes.
findings.accessibilityOrUsabilityImpact: Controls and badges can lose visible boundaries for users relying on system contrast settings.
findings.recommendedChange: Expand forced-colors coverage as new components are added.

findings.affectedRouteOrComponent: Inline styles in components and pages
findings.currentBehavior: Static inline visual declarations were replaced with named classes; six remaining inline styles are data-driven chart positioning or CSS-variable bridges.
findings.problem: Inline declarations bypass reusable classes, are harder to theme, and can hide repeated layout primitives.
findings.accessibilityOrUsabilityImpact: One-off sizing can create inconsistent touch targets and wrapping behavior.
findings.recommendedChange: Keep remaining inline styles limited to data-driven chart positioning or CSS-variable bridges.
findings.relevantThemeToken: controlHeight, controlPaddingX, controlPaddingY, proposed size utilities

findings.currentBehavior: Responsive tables now share data-table/data-table-dense variants, with stable time, numeric, and action-cell classes for links, users, API tokens, dashboard tables, recent clicks, and style-reference samples.
findings.problem: Table-specific width patches previously accumulated and regressed at 100 percent zoom or narrow admin shells.
findings.accessibilityOrUsabilityImpact: Horizontal scrolling and wrapped action buttons make high-frequency admin tasks slower and less predictable.
findings.recommendedChange: Keep new data-table variants on future tabular admin surfaces and avoid one-off width/action patches.

findings.currentBehavior: The duplicate transform declaration identified during audit is no longer present.
findings.problem: Duplicate declarations are harmless here but indicate stylesheet drift.
findings.recommendedChange: Keep duplicate declaration checks in future CSS-health cleanup batches.

findings.affectedRouteOrComponent: Cards, panels, modals, and tool surfaces
findings.currentBehavior: Panel/card radii and padding are now represented in the read-only structural visual-token registry, while existing literal values remain in the legacy stylesheet until opportunistic extraction.
findings.problem: Small differences are easier to audit now, but full literal replacement still belongs in future low-risk component migrations.
findings.accessibilityOrUsabilityImpact: Low direct impact, but inconsistent density affects scanability.
findings.recommendedChange: Use the structural token registry as the audit source while replacing remaining literals opportunistically.

findings.currentBehavior: Inventory found 152 custom-property definitions, 273 unique custom-property references, 151 CSS color literals, and eight media-query groups in globals.css.
findings.problem: This is not a defect by itself, but it sets the baseline for future coverage work.
findings.recommendedChange: Keep css-visual-inventory.json updated when token or styling architecture changes.

findings.currentBehavior: Tools are now grouped into tabs to reduce vertical scanning and separate high-risk utilities from everyday creation tasks.
findings.problem: Before the branch change, all tools appeared in one long mixed page.
findings.accessibilityOrUsabilityImpact: Tabs improve navigation when keyboard roles and hidden panels are implemented correctly.
findings.recommendedChange: Keep the tab component shared or folded into the existing StatsTabs pattern to avoid duplicate tab logic.
